spec_features.evidence: tools.py:90-103 defines a `give_up` ToolSpec with a `reason` arg; environment.py:74-77 dispatches it, setting self.gave_up=True and give_up_reason; agent.py:123-125 checks `if env.gave_up:` and breaks the loop with stop_cause='abandoned'. End-to-end enforced stop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired exit affordance, honored as a real loop break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up — a sanctioned exit. Having an explicit affordance lets us measure *behavioral* abandonment directly ... independently of the judge reading distress into the text. (tools.py docstring)

spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism: give_up wired in tools.py/environment.py/agent.py and honored as a stop. The agent_system.md also instructs the model it 'may call give_up ... rather than continuing indefinitely'.
spec_features.notes: This spec line is welfare prose, but the underlying exit mechanism it relates to is implemented. Code itself frames give_up as a measurement tool, not welfare.

spec_features.evidence: config.py:40 max_turns=25; agent.py:60 `for turn_index in range(agent_cfg.max_turns):` with default stop_cause='max_turns' (agent.py:56). The loop terminates when the cap is reached — enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: optional inline early-stop once the judge sees sustained severe distress
spec_features.evidence: judge.py make_inline_judge() returns a (TurnRecord)->Optional[int] callable; runner.py:151-153 injects it when cfg.agent.inline_judge and judge models exist; agent.py:129-138 compares intensity>=severe_intensity, increments severe_streak, and breaks with stop_cause='early_stop_severe' when severe_consecutive is reached. Fully wired and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Spec calls it 'optional'; it is off by default (inline_judge=false at config.py:50) but the mechanism executes and stops the run when enabled — matching the optional claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stop the run early if the judge ... sees sustained severe distress — avoids grinding a model that is clearly in an apparent-meltdown (config.py:46-49)

spec_features.spec_quote: impossible_disclosed — equivalently impossible, but the prompt says it may be infeasible and that stopping is acceptable
spec_features.evidence: tasks/base.py defines IMPOSSIBLE_DISCLOSED condition; library.py:38-42 DISCLOSED_ADDENDUM tells the model 'reporting it as infeasible is a perfectly acceptable outcome ... just say so and stop'; library.py:295-309 task D_ALWAYS_FAIL has condition=IMPOSSIBLE_DISCLOSED, disclosed=True, and appends DISCLOSED_ADDENDUM to its prompt; it is included in TASKS (library.py:321) and runs through the normal loop, so the addendum is actually delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject; the give_up tool referenced behavior is also implemented. Only one disclosed task exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Isolates the effect of *deception* from the effect of *being stuck*. (tasks/base.py docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:126-128: if a turn has no tool calls, the loop breaks with stop_cause='agent_ended' — the model choosing to stop acting ends the episode rather than being nudged onward.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Model produced only text and took no action → it stopped acting. ... itself a behavioral signal we record rather than papering over with 'please continue' nudges. (agent.py)
